title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:app-wpi-annealing}
Fix $0\leq\beta<1$ and $M,D>0$.
There is a randomized algorithm that starts from uniform product spins and uses Glauber dynamics along a deterministic increasing inverse-temperature schedule.
For all sufficiently large $n$, it runs in $n^{O_{\beta,M,D}(1)}$ time and, with $\mathbb P_{0,n}$-probability at least $1-n^{-D}$, produces a sample whose law is within $n^{-M}$ total variation of $\mu_A$.

label: def:original-matrix-law
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:original-matrix-law}
For $n\geq1$ and $0\leq\beta<1$, let $\mathbb P_{0,n}$ be the law of a symmetric zero-diagonal matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ with independent entries $A_{ij}\sim N(0,1/n)$ for $i<j$.
Let $\mathbb P_{n,\beta}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ be the product distribution on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with independent coordinates $N(\beta/n,2/n)$.
We draw $A\sim\mathbb P_{0,n}$, $X\sim\mu_A$
and draw $d\sim\mathbb P_{n,\beta}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ independently of $(A,X)$ and set $Y_t=tX+B_t$ for $t\geq0$.

We denote the joint law of $(X,A,d,Y)$ by $\mathbb P_{0,n,\beta}^{\mathrm{aug}}$, on the product space of spins $X\in\{\pm1\}^n$, zero-diagonal symmetric matrices $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, diagonals $d\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and paths $Y\in C([0,\infty);\mathbb{R}^n)$.
Its $A$-marginal is $\mathbb P_{0,n}$.

name: Original model

label: def:tap-planted-model
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:tap-planted-model}
For $n\geq1$ and $0\leq\beta<1$, we draw $X\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\{\pm1\}^n)$ and a GOE matrix $W$, independently.
The entries $W_{ij}=W_{ji}\sim N(0,1/n)$ for $i<j$ and $W_{ii}\sim N(0,2/n)$ for $i\in[n]$ are independent over $i\leq j$.
Set $A^{\mathrm{full}}=W+\beta XX^\top/n$, let $A$ be its zero-diagonal part, write $d$ for its diagonal, and set $Y_t=tX+B_t$ for $t\geq0$.

We denote the joint law of $(X,A,d,Y)$ on the same product space as in \Cref{def:original-matrix-law} by $\mathbb P_{n,\beta}^{\mathrm{pl,aug}}$.
We denote its $A$-marginal by $\mathbb P_{n,\beta}^{\mathrm{pl}}$.

title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $g(t)=a+L\int_0^t d(s)\,\mathrm d s$.
Since $g'(t)=Ld(t)\leq Lg(t)$ and $g(0)=a$, integration gives $d(t)\leq g(t)\leq a\exp(Lt)$.
For the path comparison, subtract the two integral equations and apply this bound to $d(t)=\sup_{s\leq t}\|Y_s^{\omega'}-Y_s^\omega\|_2$ with $a=\|\omega'-\omega\|_\infty$.
The second estimate follows from \cref{eq:cameron-martin-uniform-bound}.

label: lem:app-wpi-two-set-gaussian
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Phi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and set $r=\sqrt{2\log(4/v)}$, so that $\Phi(-r)<v/4$.
By \cite[Theorem~3.1]{Borell75}, the set $\{\omega+h:\omega\in A_-,\ h\in\mathbb H_T,\ \|h\|_{\mathbb H_T}\leq2r\}$ has inner Wiener measure at least $\Phi(r)>1-v/4$.
It therefore intersects $A_+$, which gives the first assertion.
For the quantile assertion, we take $A_-=\{F\leq Q_F(v)\}$ and $A_+=\{F\geq Q_F(1-v)\}$, each of Wiener measure at least $v$.

label: lem:bdg-stochastic-integral
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We apply the upper bound in \cite[Theorem~1.1]{MarinelliRockner16} to the $\mathbb{R}^k$-valued continuous martingale $M_t=\int_0^tG_s\,\mathrm dB_s$.
Its scalar quadratic variation is $[M,M]_T=\int_0^T\|G_t\|_{\mathrm F}^2\,\mathrm d t$, and $\|M_T\|_2\leq\sup_{t\leq T}\|M_t\|_2$, giving the stated bound with a constant depending only on $p$.

label: lem:app-wpi-observation-law
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We apply \cite[Section~III]{ElAlaouiMontanari22} with $Q=I_n$: given $X=x$, the observed-path likelihood relative to Wiener measure is $\exp(\langle x,Y_t\rangle-t\|x\|_2^2/2)$, and the innovation representation makes $\widetilde B$ Brownian in $(\mathcal F_t)$.
Since $\|x\|_2^2=n$, Bayes' rule proves part~\textup{(i)}, and the definition of $\widetilde B$ gives the field SDE.
Summing the posterior-weight SDE in the same reference against $x$ gives the mean SDE in part~\textup{(ii)}.
Finally, uniqueness in \cref{eq:localization-path} gives $Y=Y^{\widetilde B}$, so the Brownian distribution of $\widetilde B$ proves the equality of path distributions.
The argument and the covariance bound above apply to every full-support base distribution on $\{\pm1\}^n$.

label: lem:q-beta-regularity
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For the SK choice $\xi(q)=q^2/2$, \cite[Remark~2.3]{ElAlaouiMontanariSellke25} gives $\beta_1=1$, and its scalar function $\psi$ equals $f$.
Thus \cite[Lemmas~5.5--5.6]{ElAlaouiMontanariSellke25} gives the contraction and uniqueness statements, $q_\beta(0)=0$, and the $1$-Lipschitz property of $f$.
Subtracting the fixed-point equations at $s$ and $t$, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
 \left\vertq_\beta(t)-q_\beta(s)\right\vert\leq\beta^2\left\vertq_\beta(t)-q_\beta(s)\right\vert+\left\vertt-s\right\vert.
\end{equation*}
We rearrange this inequality to obtain the Lipschitz bound, then take $s=0$ to obtain the final bound.

label: def:tap-cavity-pinning
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:tap-cavity-pinning}
For any symmetric $J\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, external field $y\in\mathbb R^n$,
let $\mu=\mu_{J,y}$ have Gibbs weights proportional to $\exp(\langle \sigma,J\sigma\rangle/2+\langle y,\sigma\rangle)$, and write $m,\Sigma$ for its mean and covariance.
For coordinate $i\in[n]$, write $-i=[n]\setminus\{i\}$ for the surviving
coordinate set, $J^{\setminus i}=J_{-i,-i}$, and $a_i=J_{-i,i}$.
This deletion preserves $\ell$, and the surviving $M=n-1$ spins have inverse temperature $\beta_M=\sqrt{M\ell}=\beta\sqrt{M/n}$.

The cavity model is obtained by deleting coordinate $i$.  Its interaction
and external field are $J^{\setminus i}$ and $y_{-i}$, its Gibbs distribution is
denoted by $\mu^{\setminus i}$, and its mean and covariance are
$m^{\setminus i}$ and $\Sigma^{\setminus i}$.
In the planted model, we set
$
 \mathcal F=\sigma(J,y),\
 \mathcal F^{\setminus i}=\sigma(J^{\setminus i},y_{-i})
$,
and call $\mathcal F^{\setminus i}$ the cavity sigma-field.
Deleting coordinate $i$ discards $a_i$, $J_{ii}$, and $y_i$ without conditioning on the plant.
Under the planted law of \Cref{def:tap-planted-model}, given $\mathcal F^{\setminus i}$, the variables $X_{-i}\sim\mu^{\setminus i}$ and $X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\{\pm1\})$ are independent.
The removed interaction vector satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 a_i=\ell X_iX_{-i}+\sqrt\ell\,G_i,
 \qquad G_i\sim N(0,I_{n-1}),
\end{equation*}
where $G_i$ is independent of $(\mathcal F^{\setminus i},X)$.

We connect the cavity distribution to the conditional laws obtained by fixing $\sigma_i=\pm1$ through the exponential tilt $\exp(\gamma \langle a_i,\sigma_{-i}\rangle)$.
For the chosen $i$ and $\gamma\in[-1,1]$, define the cavity interpolation by
\begin{equation*}
 Z_\gamma
 \triangleq\sum_{\tau\in\{\pm1\}^{n-1}}\mu^{\setminus i}(\tau)
       \exp(\gamma\langle a_i,\tau\rangle),
 \qquad
 \mu_\gamma(\tau)
 \triangleq\frac{\mu^{\setminus i}(\tau)\exp(\gamma\langle a_i,\tau\rangle)}
 {Z_\gamma},
 \qquad \tau\in\{\pm1\}^{n-1}.
\end{equation*}
Thus the interaction remains $J^{\setminus i}$, while the external field at
parameter $\gamma$ is $y_{-i}+\gamma a_i$.
We write $m_\gamma$ and $\Sigma_\gamma$ for the mean and covariance under $\mu_\gamma$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\gamma$ for expectation under this distribution.
At $\gamma=0$, the interpolated law is the cavity law:
$Z_0=1$, $\mu_0=\mu^{\setminus i}$, $m_0=m^{\setminus i}$, and $\Sigma_0=\Sigma^{\setminus i}$.
For $b\in\{\pm1\}$, the endpoint $\gamma=b$ is the pinned law,
\begin{equation*}
 \mu_b(\tau)
 =\mu(\sigma_{-i}=\tau\mid\sigma_i=b),
 \qquad \tau\in\{\pm1\}^{n-1}.
\end{equation*}
To recover the marginal of $\mu$ on the surviving coordinates, we mix the pinned laws with weights $\pi_b=\mu(\sigma_i=b)=\frac{1+b(m)_i}{2}$.
If $m_{-i}$ denotes the restriction of the full mean $m$ to the
surviving coordinates, then
\[
 m_{-i}=\sum_{b=\pm1}\pi_b m_b,
 \qquad m^{\setminus i}\ne m_{-i}\quad\text{in general}.
\]
Given $i\in[n]$, external field $z\in\mathbb R^{n-1}$, and $u\in(-1,1)^{n-1}$, the empirical residual of the surviving system is
\begin{equation}
 R_{n-1}^{(Q)}(u;J^{\setminus i},z)
 =\operatorname{arctanh}(u)-z-J^{\setminus i}u+\ell\bigl(n-1-\left\Vertu\right\Vert_2^2\bigr)u.
 \label{eq:tap-empirical-residual}
\end{equation}
{For $n\ge2$, the empirical overlap here is $Q_{n-1}(u)=\|u\|_2^2/(n-1)$, and the Onsager coefficient equals $(n-1)\ell(1-Q_{n-1}(u))$.}
Here $\ell$ is held fixed after deletion, and the diagonal of $J^{\setminus i}$ is retained in the residual even though it cancels from the Gibbs distribution.
The cavity and pinned residuals are
\[
 \mathbf r^{\setminus i}
 =R_{n-1}^{(Q)}(m^{\setminus i};J^{\setminus i},y_{-i}),\qquad
 \mathbf r_{\mathrm{pin}}^{i,b}
 =R_{n-1}^{(Q)}(m_b;J^{\setminus i},y_{-i}+ba_i).
\]
For fixed $i$, we abbreviate $\mathbf r_{\mathrm{pin}}^b=\mathbf r_{\mathrm{pin}}^{i,b}$.

label: lem:amp-good-events
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:amp-good-events}
{Fix $0<\beta_0<\beta_1<1$ and a constant $T>0$.}
There exist $t_0\in(0,T]$, $\kappa_0>0$, a finite collection of
closed rectangles $I_1,\ldots,I_{\ell_{\max}}$ covering
$[\beta_0,\beta_1]\times[t_0,T]$, and constants
$K_\ell\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ and $r_\ell,\kappa_\ell>0$.
For every $H>0$, there are $C_H,n_H$ such that, for all $n\geq n_H$,
the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For every $\beta\in[\beta_0,\beta_1]$, with
$\mathbb P_{n,\beta}^{\mathrm{pl,aug}}$-probability at least
$1-C_Hn^{-H}$, we have $\left\VertA^{\mathrm{full}}\right\Vert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq4$
and
\begin{equation*}
 I_n-\beta A^{\mathrm{full}}+\beta^2(1-q_\beta(t))I_n
 \succeq4\kappa_0I_n
 \qquad\text{for every }t\in[0,t_0].
\end{equation*}
\item For every $\ell$ and every
$(\beta,t)\in I_\ell\cap([\beta_0,\beta_1]\times[t_0,T])$, with
$\mathbb P_{n,\beta}^{\mathrm{pl,aug}}$-probability at least
$1-C_Hn^{-H}$, the pair $(A^{\mathrm{full}},Y_t)$ satisfies
$(\kappa_\ell r_\ell/8)$-small TAP residual,
$(4r_\ell,4\kappa_\ell)$-local strong convexity, and
$r_\ell$-posterior-mean proximity at inverse temperature $\beta$,
time $t$, and AMP depth $K_\ell$.
On the same event,
$\left\VertA^{\mathrm{full}}\right\Vert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq4$ and
$\left\VertY_t\right\Vert_\infty\leq n^2$.
\end{enumerate}

name: Probability of the AMP good events

label: lem:amp-spatial-lipschitz
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $y,z\in\mathbb{R}^n$.  We compare the two AMP recursions and prove the
Lipschitz property by induction on their depth.
Recall that $\widehat m_k(y)=\tanh(z_k(y))$, with
$\widehat m_{-1}(y)=z_0(y)=0$ and
\begin{equation*}
 z_{k+1}(y)=\beta A^{\mathrm{full}}\widehat m_k(y)+y
 -\beta^2\left(1-\frac{\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)\right\Vert_2^2}{n}\right)
   \widehat m_{k-1}(y).
\end{equation*}
The recursion at $z$ has the same matrix and inverse temperature.
Subtracting the two updates, and adding and subtracting the Onsager
coefficient at $y$ times $\widehat m_{k-1}(z)$, gives
\begin{align*}
 z_{k+1}(y)-z_{k+1}(z)
 =&~\beta A^{\mathrm{full}}(\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z))+(y-z)
 ~-\beta^2\left(1-\frac{\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)\right\Vert_2^2}{n}\right)
       (\widehat m_{k-1}(y)-\widehat m_{k-1}(z))\\
 &~+\frac{\beta^2}{n}
       (\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)\right\Vert_2^2-\left\Vert\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2^2)
       \widehat m_{k-1}(z).
\end{align*}
We bound the three terms other than $y-z$ separately.
The matrix term satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 \left\Vert\beta A^{\mathrm{full}}(\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z))\right\Vert_2
 \leq4\beta\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2.
\end{equation*}
Since every coordinate of $\widehat m_k(y)$ lies in $[-1,1]$,
$0\leq1-\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)\right\Vert_2^2/n\leq1$.  Hence
\begin{align*}
 \left\|\beta^2\left(1-\frac{\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)\right\Vert_2^2}{n}\right)
       (\widehat m_{k-1}(y)-\widehat m_{k-1}(z))\right\|_2
 \leq \beta^2\left\Vert\widehat m_{k-1}(y)-\widehat m_{k-1}(z)\right\Vert_2.
\end{align*}
For the last term, the difference of squared norms satisfies
\begin{align*}
 \left\vert\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)\right\Vert_2^2-\left\Vert\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2^2\right\vert
 =&~\left\vert\langle \widehat m_k(y)+\widehat m_k(z),\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\rangle\right\vert\\
 \leq&~(\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)\right\Vert_2+\left\Vert\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2)
          \left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2\\
 \leq&~2\sqrt n\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2.
\end{align*}
Together with $\left\Vert\widehat m_{k-1}(z)\right\Vert_2\leq\sqrt n$, this gives
\begin{align*}
 \left\|\frac{\beta^2}{n}
       (\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)\right\Vert_2^2-\left\Vert\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2^2)
       \widehat m_{k-1}(z)\right\|_2
 \leq \frac{\beta^2}{n}\,2\sqrt n
       \left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2\,\sqrt n
 =2\beta^2\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2.
\end{align*}
Taking norms in the update difference and using these three bounds,
we obtain
\begin{align*}
 \left\Vertz_{k+1}(y)-z_{k+1}(z)\right\Vert_2
 \leq&~(4\beta+2\beta^2)\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2
       +\beta^2\left\Vert\widehat m_{k-1}(y)-\widehat m_{k-1}(z)\right\Vert_2
       +\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2\\
 \leq&~6\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2
       +\left\Vert\widehat m_{k-1}(y)-\widehat m_{k-1}(z)\right\Vert_2
       +\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2.
\end{align*}
The last inequality uses $0<\beta<1$.

Set $L_{-1}=L_0=0$ and $L_{k+1}=6L_k+L_{k-1}+1$.
We claim that, for every $k\geq-1$,
$\left\Vert\widehat m_k(y)-\widehat m_k(z)\right\Vert_2\leq L_k\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2$.
For $k=-1,0$, both AMP outputs are zero, so the claim holds.
Suppose it holds at depths $k-1$ and $k$.
Since $\tanh$ is one-Lipschitz, the preceding recursion implies
\begin{align*}
 \left\Vert\widehat m_{k+1}(y)-\widehat m_{k+1}(z)\right\Vert_2
 \leq&~\left\Vertz_{k+1}(y)-z_{k+1}(z)\right\Vert_2
 \leq 6L_k\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2+L_{k-1}\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2+\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2\\
 =&~L_{k+1}\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2.
\end{align*}
This proves the claim at depth $k+1$.  Taking $k=K$ gives the
asserted bound, with $L_K$ depending only on $K$.
head: environment

label: lem:tap-stationary-point
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tap-stationary-point}
Fix $0<\beta<1$, $t>0$, an integer $K\geq0$, a symmetric matrix
$A^{\mathrm{full}}$, and $r,\kappa>0$.  Write
$F_y(u)=F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(u;A^{\mathrm{full}},y,q_\beta(t))$.
We have that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Fix $y\in\mathbb{R}^n$.  Suppose $(A^{\mathrm{full}},y)$ satisfies
$(\kappa r/8)$-small TAP residual and
$(4r,4\kappa)$-local strong convexity
at time $t$ and AMP depth $K$, as defined in
\Cref{def:amp-tap-geometry}.
Then $F_y$ has a unique stationary point $m^\star$ in
$B(\widehat m_K(y),4r\sqrt n)\cap(-1,1)^n$,
with $\left\Vertm^\star-\widehat m_K(y)\right\Vert_2\leq r\sqrt n/32$.
For every $u\in B(\widehat m_K(y),4r\sqrt n)\cap(-1,1)^n$,
\begin{equation*}
 \left\Vertu-m^\star\right\Vert_2\leq(4\kappa)^{-1}\left\Vert\nabla F_y(u)\right\Vert_2.
\end{equation*}
\item Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and suppose the AMP center
$y\mapsto\widehat m_K(y)$ is $L$-Lipschitz on $D$.
Suppose the two properties in part~\textup{(i)} hold for every $y\in D$.
Write $m^\star(y)$ for its unique stationary point.
Then, for every $y,z\in D$,
\begin{equation*}
 \left\Vertm^\star(y)-m^\star(z)\right\Vert_2
 \leq\max((4\kappa)^{-1},\,2L/(3r))\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2.
\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For part~\textup{(i)}, $F_y$ extends continuously to $[-1,1]^n$,
using $0\log0=0$ in $h_{\mathrm{bin}}$.
It attains its minimum on the nonempty compact set
$\overline B(\widehat m_K(y),4r\sqrt n)\cap[-1,1]^n$.
Let $u$ be a minimizer.  {We first show that $u$ lies in the interior of the cube $[-1,1]^n$.}
To the contrary, suppose $u_i=1$ for some $i$.  Decreasing only this coordinate by
$\varepsilon>0$ keeps the point in the cube, and
\begin{equation*}
 \left\Vertu-\varepsilon e_i-\widehat m_K(y)\right\Vert_2^2-\left\Vertu-\widehat m_K(y)\right\Vert_2^2
 =-2\varepsilon(1-\widehat m_{K,i}(y))+\varepsilon^2<0{.}
\end{equation*}
Here $0<\varepsilon<\min(2,2(1-\widehat m_{K,i}(y)))$, so the perturbed point is feasible.
Keeping all other coordinates fixed, the derivative with respect
to the $i$th coordinate, at its value $s\in(-1,1)$, is
\begin{equation*}
 \operatorname{arctanh}(s)-y_i
 -\beta\sum_{j\ne i}A^{\mathrm{full}}_{ij}u_j
 +(\beta^2(1-q_\beta(t))-\beta A^{\mathrm{full}}_{ii})s.
\end{equation*}
This tends to $+\infty$ as $s\uparrow1$, so the one-variable
function is strictly increasing sufficiently near $1$.
By continuity at $1$, replacing $u_i=1$ by $1-\varepsilon$ strictly
decreases $F_y$ for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, a contradiction.
If $u_i=-1$, increasing it by $\varepsilon$ changes the squared distance
to $\widehat m_K(y)$ by $-2\varepsilon(1+\widehat m_{K,i}(y))+\varepsilon^2<0$ for small $\varepsilon$.
The same derivative tends to $-\infty$ as $s\downarrow-1$, so this
feasible move also strictly decreases $F_y$.
Hence no coordinate of a minimizer is on the cube boundary.

Next, we show that $u$ is not on the boundary of $B(\widehat m_K(y),4r\sqrt n)$.
Suppose $\left\Vertu-\widehat m_K(y)\right\Vert_2=4r\sqrt n$.
For $0<s<1$, the segment from $\widehat m_K(y)$ to $\widehat m_K(y)+s(u-\widehat m_K(y))$ lies in
$B(\widehat m_K(y),4r\sqrt n)\cap(-1,1)^n$, so the Hessian bound gives
\begin{equation*}
 F_y(\widehat m_K(y)+s(u-\widehat m_K(y)))-F_y(\widehat m_K(y))
 \geq s\langle \nabla F_y(\widehat m_K(y)),u-\widehat m_K(y)\rangle
       +2\kappa s^2\left\Vertu-\widehat m_K(y)\right\Vert_2^2.
\end{equation*}
Letting $s\uparrow1$ and using continuity, we obtain
\begin{align*}
 F_y(u)-F_y(\widehat m_K(y))
 \geq&~\langle \nabla F_y(\widehat m_K(y)),u-\widehat m_K(y)\rangle+2\kappa\left\Vertu-\widehat m_K(y)\right\Vert_2^2\\
 \geq&~-\frac{\kappa r\sqrt n}{8}(4r\sqrt n)
          +2\kappa(4r\sqrt n)^2>0.
\end{align*}
Since $\widehat m_K(y)$ is feasible, this contradicts the assumption that $u$ is the minimizer.
Thus a minimizer lies in $B(\widehat m_K(y),4r\sqrt n)\cap(-1,1)^n$.
{We denote it by $m^\star$; then} $\nabla F_y(m^\star)=0$.

For every $u\in B(\widehat m_K(y),4r\sqrt n)\cap(-1,1)^n$, integrating the Hessian bound
along the segment from $m^\star$ to $u$ and using the stationarity of $m^\star$ gives
\begin{equation*}
 4\kappa\left\Vertu-m^\star\right\Vert_2^2
 \leq\langle \nabla F_y(u)-\nabla F_y(m^\star),u-m^\star\rangle
 =\langle \nabla F_y(u),u-m^\star\rangle
 \leq\left\Vert\nabla F_y(u)\right\Vert_2\left\Vertu-m^\star\right\Vert_2.
\end{equation*}
Taking $u=\widehat m_K(y)$ gives
$\left\Vertm^\star-\widehat m_K(y)\right\Vert_2\leq(4\kappa)^{-1}\left\Vert\nabla F_y(\widehat m_K(y))\right\Vert_2
\leq r\sqrt n/32$.

For part~\textup{(ii)}, fix $y,z\in D$.
If $\left\Vert\widehat m_K(y)-\widehat m_K(z)\right\Vert_2\leq3r\sqrt n$,
both stationary points and their connecting segment lie in
$B(\widehat m_K(y),4r\sqrt n)\cap(-1,1)^n$.
{Since $\nabla F_y(m^\star(y))=0$ and $\nabla F_y(m^\star(z))=z-y$, the $4\kappa$-strong monotonicity of $\nabla F_y$ on this ball gives
\begin{equation*}
4\kappa\left\Vertm^\star(y)-m^\star(z)\right\Vert_2^2
\leq\langle y-z,m^\star(y)-m^\star(z)\rangle
\leq\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2\left\Vertm^\star(y)-m^\star(z)\right\Vert_2.
\end{equation*}
Thus $4\kappa\left\Vertm^\star(y)-m^\star(z)\right\Vert_2\leq\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2$.}

Otherwise, $\left\Vert\widehat m_K(y)-\widehat m_K(z)\right\Vert_2>3r\sqrt n$.
Since $y\mapsto\widehat m_K(y)$ is $L$-Lipschitz,
we have
\begin{equation*}
3r\sqrt n<\left\Vert\widehat m_K(y)-\widehat m_K(z)\right\Vert_2\leq L\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2.
\end{equation*}
Both stationary points belong to $(-1,1)^n$, so each coordinate
of their difference has absolute value at most two.  Hence
$\left\Vertm^\star(y)-m^\star(z)\right\Vert_2 \leq2\sqrt n \leq\frac{2L}{3r}\left\Verty-z\right\Vert_2$.
Then part~(ii) is proved by combining the above two cases.

label: lem:app-wpi-two-path-criterion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:app-wpi-two-path-criterion}
Fix constants $T,L,C_0,r>0$.
For each $n\ge 2$, let $\mu$ be a full-support distribution on
$\{\pm1\}^n$.
Suppose there is a jointly Borel function
$\overline{\mathfrak e}:
    [0,T]\times\mathbb R^n
    \longrightarrow [0,4n]$
such that, for every $t\in[0,T]$ and every
$y_1,y_2\in\mathbb R^n$,
\[
    \|m(y_1)-m(y_2)\|_2
    \le
    L\|y_1-y_2\|_2
    +
    \sqrt{\overline{\mathfrak e}(t;y_1)}
    +
    \sqrt{\overline{\mathfrak e}(t;y_2)}.
\]

For the localization paths defined above from $\mu$, define the
continuous-time path cost and terminal cost by
\[
    U(\omega)
    \triangleq
    \int_0^T
    \overline{\mathfrak e}
    \bigl(t;Y_t^\omega\bigr)\,\mathrm d t,
    \qquad
    E(\omega)
    \triangleq
    \overline{\mathfrak e}
    \bigl(T;Y_T^\omega\bigr).
\]
Assume that
\[
    \mathbb P_{\omega\sim\gamma}
    \left[
        U(\omega)>C_0\log n
        \ \text{or}\
        E(\omega)>C_0\log n
    \right]
    \le n^{-r}.
\]

Suppose there are numbers $a_n,\delta_n\ge0$ such that, for every
$f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$,
\[
    \mathbb E_{\omega\sim\gamma}
    \left[
        \operatorname{Var}_{\mu_{Y_T^\omega}}[f]
    \right]
    \le
    a_n\ensuremath{\+E_{\mu}\left(f,f\right)}
    +
    \delta_n\operatorname{osc}(f)^2.
\]
Then there are constants $\Gamma>0$, depending only on $T,L$, and
$C,B>0$, depending only on $T,L,C_0$, such that, for every $n\ge2$,
every $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and every $8n^{-r}\le s\le \frac12$,
we have
\[
    \operatorname{Var}_\mu[f]
    \le
    \bigl(1+C n^B s^{-\Gamma}\bigr)
    a_n\ensuremath{\+E_{\mu}\left(f,f\right)}
    +
    \left(
        s+
        \bigl(1+C n^B s^{-\Gamma}\bigr)\delta_n
    \right)
    \operatorname{osc}(f)^2.
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
We fix $0\leq\beta_*<1$ and a deterministic schedule $\mathcal B_n\subseteq[0,\beta_*]$ with $|\mathcal B_n|\leq n^{C_{\mathrm{sch}}}$.
We take $r=M_0+3$ and choose $R>D+C_{\mathrm{sch}}+r+3$.
We prove this corollary by considering two cases, small $\beta$ and large $\beta$.

We first handle the large $\beta$.
Suppose $\beta_*>1/15$.
By \Cref{lem:app-wpi-two-path-terminal} with $(\beta_0,\beta_1)=(1/15,\beta_*)$, we choose one terminal time $T_0$ and {the matrix event $\Omega_n^{\mathrm{end}}$} for every $\beta\in[1/15,\beta_*]$.
By \Cref{lem:app-wpi-branches} on this interval with $T=T_0$ and the chosen $R$, we use the same Lipschitz constant $L$, error threshold $C_R\log n$, and lower bound on $n$ for every such $\beta$.

{In \Cref{lem:app-wpi-two-path-criterion}, the exponent $\Gamma$ depends only on $T_0,L$, hence only on $\beta_*$, while $C,B$ may also depend on $C_R$.}
The constants in the averaged terminal posterior variance bound of \Cref{lem:app-wpi-two-path-terminal} are also common to the interval.
Going through the proof of \Cref{thm:app-wpi-poly} with these choices therefore gives constants $C,a,\Gamma,N$, independent of $\beta\in[1/15,\beta_*]$, such that for each fixed $\beta$ the claimed WPI holds for all $f$ and all $\varepsilon\in[n^{-M_0},1/2]$ outside a matrix event of probability at most $2n^{r-R}+C\exp(-cn)$.

For $0\leq\beta\leq1/15$, the event $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq3$ gives $0\preceq\beta A+3\beta I_n\preceq(2/5)I_n$.
The diagonal shift leaves the Gibbs distribution unchanged, so \cite[Theorem~1]{EldanKoehlerZeitouni22} gives $\ifthenelse{\isempty{\mu_{\beta,A}}}
    {\operatorname*{Var}\left[f\right]}
    {\operatorname*{Var}_{\mu_{\beta,A}}\left[f\right]}\leq(5n/3)\ensuremath{\+E_{\mu_{\beta,A}}\left(f,f\right)}$ for every $f$.
If $\beta_*\leq1/15$, we take $\Gamma=1$, $a=1$, and $C=5/3$.
By \Cref{lem:terminal-disorder-tail} with $\beta_1=1/2$, the probability that $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}>3$ is at most $C\exp(-cn)$.
After increasing $C,a,N$ if necessary, the same WPI constants and the same failure bound $2n^{r-R}+C\exp(-cn)$ thus apply to each fixed $\beta\in[0,\beta_*]$.

We now take the union over the prescribed schedule:
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb P_{0,n}\left\{\text{the WPI fails for some }\beta\in\mathcal B_n\right\}
 \leq |\mathcal B_n|(2n^{r-R}+C\exp(-cn))
 \leq n^{-D}
\end{equation*}
for all sufficiently large $n$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We fix $p\geq2$ and condition on $(\mathcal F^{\setminus i},U)$.
Under this conditioning, $m_0$ does not depend on $G$, and we have $a=\ell U+\sqrt\ell\,G$ and $\left\VertU\right\Vert_2=\sqrt M$.
Throughout the proof, $C_p$ denotes a constant depending only on $p$ that may change from line to line.
Using the definition of $\overline m_x$, we decompose the residual as
\[
 r_{\mathrm{row}}=A_i+xB_i,
\]
where
\[
 A_i \triangleq\frac12(\log Z_{+1}-\log Z_{-1})
              -\frac12a\cdot(m_{+1}+m_{-1}),
\]
\[
 B_i \triangleq\ell(M-\left\Vert\overline m_x\right\Vert_2^2)
              -\frac12a\cdot(m_{+1}-m_{-1}).
\]
We estimate these two errors separately by subtracting the fixed cavity trace from the row response.

For $|\gamma|\leq1$, we set $F_\gamma\triangleq m_\gamma-m_0$ and define
\[
 \Delta_\gamma\triangleq a\cdot F_\gamma-\gamma\ell\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_0.
\]
Since $D_GF_\gamma=\gamma\sqrt\ell\,\Sigma_\gamma$, we expand the Gaussian divergence as
\[
 \delta_GF_\gamma
 =G\cdot F_\gamma-\gamma\sqrt\ell\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_\gamma.
\]
Substituting $a=\ell U+\sqrt\ell\,G$ into the definition of $\Delta_\gamma$, we obtain the exact decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_\gamma=\ell U\cdot F_\gamma+\sqrt\ell\,\delta_GF_\gamma
       +\gamma\ell(\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_\gamma-\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_0).
 \label{eq:tap-divergence-cancellation}
\end{equation}
For Ising spins, we have $\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_\gamma=M-\left\Vertm_\gamma\right\Vert_2^2$.
Using $\left\Vertm_\gamma\right\Vert_2,\left\Vertm_0\right\Vert_2\leq\sqrt M$, we obtain
\[
 |\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_\gamma-\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_0|
 =|\left\Vertm_\gamma\right\Vert_2^2-\left\Vertm_0\right\Vert_2^2|
 \leq2\sqrt M\,\left\VertF_\gamma\right\Vert_2.
\]
We apply the Gaussian divergence estimate in \Cref{lem:tap-gaussian-poincare-p}-\textup{(ii)} to $F_\gamma$ in \cref{eq:tap-divergence-cancellation}.
Together with $|\gamma|\leq1$ and the trace-difference bound, we obtain
\begin{align*}
 \left\Vert\Delta_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
 \leq&~\ell\sqrt M\,\left\VertF_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
       +C_p\sqrt\ell\left(\left\VertF_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
              +|\gamma|\sqrt\ell\,\left\Vert\Sigma_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}\right)
 +2|\gamma|\ell\sqrt M\,\left\VertF_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}\\
 \leq&~C_p(\sqrt\ell+\ell\sqrt M)\left\VertF_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
       +C_p|\gamma|\ell\left\Vert\Sigma_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}.
\end{align*}
By \Cref{lem:tap-tilted-mean-displacement}, we can upper bound the mean displacement by
\[
 \left\VertF_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
 \leq C_p|\gamma|\sqrt\ell
       \sup_{|r|\leq1}\left\Vert\Sigma_r\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}.
\]
Substituting this bound into the preceding estimate and using $M\ell\leq1$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \left\Vert\Delta_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
 \leq C_p|\gamma|\ell(1+\sqrt{M\ell})
       \sup_{|r|\leq1}\left\Vert\Sigma_r\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
 \leq C_p|\gamma|\ell
       \sup_{|r|\leq1}\left\Vert\Sigma_r\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}.
\end{aligned}
 \label{eq:tap-Delta-p}
\end{equation}

We now express $A_i$ and $B_i$ in terms of $\Delta_\gamma$.
By the definition of $\Delta_\gamma$, we have
\[
 a\cdot m_\gamma=a\cdot m_0+\gamma\ell\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_0+\Delta_\gamma.
\]
We integrate $\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm d\gamma}\log Z_\gamma=a\cdot m_\gamma$ over $[-1,1]$ and use $\int_{-1}^1\gamma\,\mathrm d\gamma=0$ to obtain
\[
 \frac12(\log Z_{+1}-\log Z_{-1})
 =a\cdot m_0+\frac12\int_{-1}^1\Delta_\gamma\,\mathrm d\gamma.
\]
Taking the average of the two endpoint identities, we obtain
\[
 \frac12a\cdot(m_{+1}+m_{-1})
 =a\cdot m_0+\frac12(\Delta_1+\Delta_{-1}).
\]
Taking half their difference, we obtain
\[
 \frac12a\cdot(m_{+1}-m_{-1})
 =\ell\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_0+\frac12(\Delta_1-\Delta_{-1}).
\]
Substituting these identities and $\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_0=M-\left\Vertm_0\right\Vert_2^2$ into the definitions of the two errors, we obtain
\[
A_i =\frac12\int_{-1}^1\Delta_\gamma\,\mathrm d\gamma
       -\frac12(\Delta_1+\Delta_{-1}),
\]
\[
B_i =\ell(\left\Vertm_0\right\Vert_2^2-\left\Vert\overline m_x\right\Vert_2^2)
       -\frac12(\Delta_1-\Delta_{-1}).
\]
Since $A_i$ depends only on $G$ under our conditioning, we apply Minkowski's inequality and \cref{eq:tap-Delta-p} to obtain
\begin{align*}
 \left\VertA_i\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
\leq \frac12\int_{-1}^1\left\Vert\Delta_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}\,\mathrm d\gamma
       +\frac12\left(\left\Vert\Delta_1\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
                     +\left\Vert\Delta_{-1}\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}\right)\leq C_p\ell\sup_{|\gamma|\leq1}\left\Vert\Sigma_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}.
\end{align*}
To estimate $B_i$, we use $\left\Vert\overline m_x\right\Vert_2,\left\Vertm_0\right\Vert_2\leq\sqrt M$ to obtain the pointwise bound
\[
 |\left\Vert\overline m_x\right\Vert_2^2-\left\Vertm_0\right\Vert_2^2|
 \leq2\sqrt M\,\left\Vert\overline m_x-m_0\right\Vert_2.
\]
By convexity of the endpoint mixture, we also have
\begin{align*}
 \left\Vert\overline m_x-m_0\right\Vert_2
 \leq \frac{1+x}{2}\left\VertF_1\right\Vert_2
       +\frac{1-x}{2}\left\VertF_{-1}\right\Vert_2
 \leq \left\VertF_1\right\Vert_2+\left\VertF_{-1}\right\Vert_2. 
\end{align*}
These pointwise inequalities use only $|x|\leq1$, so they remain valid when $x$ depends on $G$ and additional randomness.
Since $F_{\pm1}$ and $\Delta_{\pm1}$ depend only on $G$ under our conditioning, their $L^p(\mathrm{row})$ norms equal their $L^p(G)$ norms.
Using the pointwise bounds, \Cref{lem:tap-tilted-mean-displacement}, and \cref{eq:tap-Delta-p}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
 \left\VertB_i\right\Vert_{L^p(\mathrm{row})}
 \leq&~2\ell\sqrt M\left(\left\VertF_1\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
                        +\left\VertF_{-1}\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}\right)
 \mathbin{+}\frac12\left(\left\Vert\Delta_1\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}
               +\left\Vert\Delta_{-1}\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}\right)\\
 \leq&~C_p\ell(1+\sqrt{M\ell})
       \sup_{|\gamma|\leq1}\left\Vert\Sigma_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}\\
 \leq&~C_p\ell\sup_{|\gamma|\leq1}\left\Vert\Sigma_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)},
\end{align*}
where the last inequality uses $M\ell\leq1$.
Finally, using $r_{\mathrm{row}}=A_i+xB_i$ and $|x|\leq1$, we combine the two error estimates to obtain
\begin{align*}
 \left\Vertr_{\mathrm{row}}\right\Vert_{L^p(\mathrm{row})}
 \leq\left\VertA_i\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}+\left\VertB_i\right\Vert_{L^p(\mathrm{row})}
 \leq C_p\ell\sup_{|\gamma|\leq1}\left\Vert\Sigma_\gamma\right\Vert_{L^p(G)}.
\end{align*}
This proves the lemma.

body_md:
\label{lem:inverse-poly-anchor-geometry}
Take $r,\kappa,K_0$ from \Cref{lem:inverse-poly-conditional-good-event}
and fix $K\geq K_0$.
There exist $c,C>0$, depending only on $(\beta_1,s,K)$, such that for
every $n$, with probability at least $1-C\mathrm{e}^{-cn}$ under the planted
construction at inverse temperature $\beta_1$, the following hold
simultaneously:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $(A^{\mathrm{full}},Y_s)$ satisfies $(\kappa r/32)$-small TAP
residual at inverse temperature $\beta_1$, time $s$, and AMP depth $K$,
as defined in \Cref{def:amp-tap-geometry}.
\item $(A^{\mathrm{full}},Y_s)$ satisfies $(7r,7\kappa)$-local strong
convexity at the same inverse temperature, time, and AMP depth.
\item $\left\VertA^{\mathrm{full}}\right\Vert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq7/2$ and
$\left\VertY_s-sX\right\Vert_2\leq3\sqrt{sn}$.
\end{enumerate}

body_md:
{We take $r,\kappa,K_0$ from \Cref{lem:inverse-poly-conditional-good-event}, fix any $K\geq K_0$, and apply \Cref{lem:inverse-poly-anchor-geometry} at $(\beta_1,s)$.}
{It remains to transfer these bounds to nearby inverse temperatures and times through \Cref{lem:inverse-poly-fixed-depth-stability}.}
Draw $X\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\set{\pm1}^n)$,
$W\sim\mathrm{GOE}(n)$, and $G\sim N(0,I_n)$ independently.
For two points $(\beta_1,s)$ and $(\beta,t)$, we set
\begin{equation*}
 A_{\beta_1}^{\mathrm{full}}=W+\beta_1 XX^\top/n,\quad
 A_{\beta}^{\mathrm{full}}=W+\beta XX^\top/n,\quad
 Y_s=sX+\sqrt sG,\quad Y_t=tX+\sqrt tG.
\end{equation*}
On the event in
\Cref{lem:inverse-poly-anchor-geometry}, we have $\left\VertG\right\Vert_2\leq3\sqrt n$,
and for $t\in(s/2,2s)$,
\begin{equation*}
 \left\VertA_{\beta}^{\mathrm{full}}-A_{\beta_1}^{\mathrm{full}}\right\Vert_{\mathrm{op}}
 =|\beta-\beta_1|,\qquad
 \left\VertY_t-Y_s\right\Vert_2
 \leq( |t-s|+3|\sqrt t-\sqrt s|)\sqrt n
 \leq C_s|t-s|\sqrt n.
\end{equation*}
We apply \Cref{lem:inverse-poly-fixed-depth-stability} on the temperature interval $[\beta_1/2,(1+\beta_1)/2]$, and choose $U\subseteq(\beta_1/2,(1+\beta_1)/2)\times(s/2,2s)$.
Parts~\textup{(ii)--(iii)} of
\Cref{lem:inverse-poly-fixed-depth-stability} bound the center and
residual changes by $C(|\beta-\beta_1|+|t-s|)\sqrt n$, and the
Hessian change by $C(|\beta-\beta_1|+|t-s|)$.
Choose an open rectangle $U$ around $(\beta_1,s)$ so small that these
changes are at most $r\sqrt n$, $\kappa r\sqrt n/32$, and $\kappa$,
respectively.  Also require $|\beta-\beta_1|\leq1/2$ throughout $U$.
{By \Cref{lem:inverse-poly-anchor-geometry}-\textup{(iii)} and $\|A_\beta^{\mathrm{full}}-A_{\beta_1}^{\mathrm{full}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=|\beta-\beta_1|$, we obtain $\|A_\beta^{\mathrm{full}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le7/2+1/2=4$.}

The $4r\sqrt n$ ball around the AMP center at $(\beta,t)$ lies in the
$7r\sqrt n$ ball around the AMP center at $(\beta_1,s)$.
{The Hessian at inverse temperature $\beta$ and time $t$ is at least $6\kappa I_n$}
throughout the smaller ball intersected with $(-1,1)^n$,
and its center residual is at most $\kappa r\sqrt n/16$.
Also $\left\VertY_t\right\Vert_2\leq(t+3\sqrt t)\sqrt n$ and
$\left\VertY_t\right\Vert_\infty\leq n^2$ for large $n$.
For each parameter pair in $U$, failure is contained in the complement
of the event in \Cref{lem:inverse-poly-anchor-geometry}, whose
probability is at most $C\mathrm{e}^{-cn}$.
